summary: Korean stocks are falling back. The KOSPI dropped 2.6% on Oct 8 to about 6,626 and is down about 6% in a month, still far below its June peak above 9,000. Foreign investors have been selling Samsung and SK Hynix, the two memory chip giants that make up much of the index. The Bank of Korea raised its rate to 3.0% in August and meets again Oct 22. Samsung and SK Hynix have no regular US listing, so US investors reach this mostly through EWY, Korean bank ADRs and Coupang.
for_you: Korea is a memory chip market. Foreign selling of Samsung and SK hynix is a warning sign for the AI memory trade (MU on the dashboard). No action, just watch whether the selling spreads to MU.
